recipes.name: Valerie’s Fruit Dip
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed
1 (3.4 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Mix together frozen whipped topping, cream cheese, vanilla pudding mix, confectioners’ sugar, and milk in a medium bowl. Serve chilled.

raw_recipe.headline: Valerie’s Fruit Dip
raw_recipe.description: An easy fruit dip made with pudding. Spear your favorite fruit on a toothpick and dip it in this fabulously easy, creamy vanilla dip recipe.
raw_recipe.name: Valerie’s Fruit Dip

1 (3.4 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

review.reviewBody: Perfect! I made sure to blend the cream cheese first until it was light and fluffy, then slowly added the milk and made sure there were no lumps. Added the rest of the ingredients, and added a tsp of vanilla for additional kick. Served with fruit kabobs. Had to make 12 copies of the recipe for everyone at the office. Warning: you will want to eat this by the spoonful!

It's so good I'm literally eating it by the spoonful, I can't help it!
The only thing I did different was adding ingredients one at a time. 
I mixed the milk into the pudding, then the cream cheese, whipped cream then the powdered sugar. I used an electric mixer and made it yesterday for a party, I didn't do it in that order and the cream cheese just didn't want to combine properly. Today I made if for my own snacking needs and it came out smooth and creamy.

Second time's a charm! The first time, I mixed everything together at once, per the instructions and although it tasted great, the dip had tons of tiny cream cheese chunks, which I didn't like. The second time, I followed the reviewers who said to cream the cream cheese first, add milk slowly and go from there. I took it one step further, and found it to be perfect. Here's what I did in order. First, mix room temperature cream cheese until creamy. Then slowly add the milk, also warmed to room temperature so the shock of cold doesn't make the cream cheese start to solidify again. I then added half of the thawed whipped topping and vanilla pudding. Followed by the confectioner's sugar and remaining whipped topping, all the while, being stirred on low to medium setting in the Kitchenaide. Voila! Perfect, creamy vanilla dip that's good enough to eat with a spoon.

This dip is so delicious! But directions definitely need to have you beat the cream cheese first to smooth it out. We put everything in the bowl and mixed it at the same time and it came out very lumpy.
Delicious! We whipped real whipped cream separately and folded it into the mixed cream cheese, vanilla pudding, sugar and milk.

A delicious way to eat more fruit. I used sugar-free vanilla pudding, light cool-whip, and light cream cheese. There is no need to add the sugar but I need include ¼ teaspoon of vanilla extract. Be sure to whip the cream cheese with the pudding and milk before adding the frozen topping. You may have to add more milk for the desired consistency. I used the following fruit: strawberries, raspberries, cantaloupe, bananas and kiwi. A big hit that evening and again for breakfast.

I made this and it was awesome. I followed the other suggestions and beat the cream cheese and milk together first to eliminate the lumps and then I reduced the sugar to a 1/2 cup. Like one of the other reviewers - I found myself just eating it by itself with a spoon! Thanks.

This was so great!Cut sugar in half. Cream milk with cream cheese until smooth;add all but cool whip. Fold in cool whip. Added a bit of marashino cherry juice for color and topped with a sprinkle of cinnamon. Looked and tasted fantastic!

I used instant sugar free CHEESECAKE pudding mix, "lite" whipped topping, reduced fat cream cheese and fat free evaporated milk. In-sane. I served it with chunked pound cake, strawberries, blackberries, chunked kiwi, and pineapple. Nothing remains. We ate it all. Thanks so much, Valerie. We LOVED this.

Loved this recipe. I cut down the confectionary sugar to keep it from being overly sweet. I made it to go with with fresh pineapple chunks ( from 2 pineapples), and cut the recipe in half. We had more than enough dip.
Use white chocolate pudding mix and chopped white chocolate chips. Smashing hit with everyone every time!
This dip is really gross and has no flavor. I added a whole jar of cherry juice to it and it still has no flavor. Would never make it again!!!
Absolutely one of the most requested foods for gatherings. They use it on fruit, on my pumpkin bread and a spoonful in the mouth. My family cannot get enough.
My cream cheese was hard to mix in without lumps but I ran it through the blender and it was perfect. Tasted delicious!

This was so simple but amazing at the same time. The kids loved it...they ate all of their fruit. I used a variety of fruits and it went with all; blueberries, raspberries,strawberries, bananas, mango. And best of all it is still amazing the next day!

I made a fruit salad with strawberries, blueberries, red grapes, & bananas sprinkled with a little sugar and lemon juice. I wanted to kick it up a notch for company by adding a fruit dip. This was a huge hit with my family - and I got bonus points with my Father-In-Law who loved it. It was creamy and very tasty. Thanks for the recipe!
This is the best fruit dip I have tried! It is my new favorite.
I made this last year for Christmas brunch and everyone loved it. It was a huge hit! Its very sweet but compliments the fruit nicely. They begged me o bring it again this year!
I absolutely love this recipe! I made it for a gathering at work and for my husband to take to work for an office party and everyone just raved about it! Thanks for sharing, Valerie!
This recipe is amazing on yellow cake
